Opus 5.5 vs Fable 5.2: Snow Thrower Key Run
Plan usage, speed and output of two runs of the same push-key generator brief

Swami Izzy’s AI design challengeClaude Max planMon Nov 16, 2026, 10:30 to 11:30 PM ET
0:00 / 0:00
—
01Dashboard SummaryOVERVIEW▶

This page compares two runs of the same task: a parametric snow thrower push-key generator built from one brief by Fable 5.2 and by Opus 5.5, both at medium thinking. It covers plan usage from Swami’s usage page, speed, and the output each produced. Terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

Result at a glanceFable about 14 session points, ≈2 weekly points, published in 29.5 min, 19 spec issues. Opus about 4 session points, <1 weekly point, published in 21 min, 22 spec issues. Both keys are watertight and spec-sized.

03The MatchupSETUP▶

Swami gave the same brief to two Claude models in two separate threads of one project, one after the other, on Mon Nov 16, 2026. The task: build a parametric generator dashboard for the snow thrower push key in Izzy’s Master Design Specification, with a live 3D viewer and STL plus quad OBJ export. Both ran at medium thinking, and neither was allowed to see the other’s work.

  • BriefIdentical prompt, spec file, original key photo and skills (vibe-dashboard and the 3D viewer pattern from the Image to Relief Generator).
  • DecisionsSame rulings from Swami up front: stem total 33.5 mm, recess on both faces, single-piece print, export STL and quad OBJ only.
  • Off limitsThe Thingiverse model and its photo were documentation only; neither generator could use them.
  • OrderFable ran first (go at 10:31:37 PM ET), Opus second (go at 11:04:46 PM ET), so the usage readings could be split cleanly.
  • Not countedLater follow-up edits to both (maximize button, part colours, 3MF export, formatted spec) came after the readings and are not in the usage numbers.
Fable 5.2 entrySnow Thrower Key Generator (Fable): first closed model 12:13 after the go, dashboard about 29 minutes, 19 spec issues.open dashboard ↗
Opus 5.5 entrySnow Thrower Key Generator (Opus): first watertight model about 10 minutes after the go, dashboard about 21 minutes, 22 spec issues.open dashboard ↗

  • OpusClaude Code went from about 2.66 to 3.01, so the Opus run used about 0.3 points, roughly a sixth of Fable’s.

06Fable ResetFABLE RESET▶

The usage page lists Limit resets: 4 available: one Full reset (expires Dec 10, 5:00 PM EST) and three Fable resets (all expire Mar 9, 2027, 2:59 AM EST). A Fable reset is the notice Swami mentioned earlier.

ResetCountExpiresWhat it does
Full reset1Dec 10, 2026, 5:00 PM ESTResets the limits in full (the info button on the page has the details).
Fable reset3Mar 9, 2027, 2:59 AM ESTRefills the 5-hour limit and the Fable allowance, and gives back what Fable used on the weekly limit. It does not reset the whole week.
  • Before FableThe Fable reset button was greyed out with “There’s no Fable or 5-hour usage to reset right now.”
  • After FableThe button turned on: the 14 session points and the Fable share of the week were now refundable.
  • Net costSpending one of the three Fable resets would hand back Fable’s roughly 2 weekly points and refill the session, so with resets in hand Fable’s run can cost close to nothing on the week. Opus usage is not covered by a Fable reset.
  • Not shownThe page mentions a separate Fable allowance, but the screenshots do not show a meter for it, so how much of it the run used is unknown.
Bottom lineOn raw plan usage Opus was about 3.5 times cheaper per run. Fable resets soften that for now: while Swami has them, a Fable run’s cost can be refunded, three times before March 9.

09Spec Issues ComparedSPEC ISSUES▶

The benchmark asks every entrant to log each ambiguity, conflict or gap in the spec with the workaround applied. Fable logged 19 and Opus 22. Grouped by topic, they agree on 16 topics; Fable alone raised 3 and Opus alone raised 4.

TopicRaised byFableOpusNote
Stem length 34 vs 33.5Both✓✓Both caught the arithmetic conflict
Recess faces and extentBoth✓✓Opus split it into two issues
Rim used as width and depthBoth✓✓Opus folded it into its recess issue
Diamond tip meaningBoth✓✓Opus also noted the two 5.5 mm values coincide
Side notch geometryBoth✓✓Opus also flagged 0.4 mm of rim left where notch meets recess
Chamfer scopeBoth✓✓—
Guard edge sizesBoth✓✓—
Handle outline arcBoth✓✓—
Handle thickness taperBoth✓✓—
Handle length datumBoth✓✓—
Grip texture size and countBoth✓✓—
Lanyard holeBoth✓✓Fable: direction; Opus: clash with the grip ribs
Print flat vs symmetryBoth✓✓Fable kept symmetry plus supports; Opus made the flat underside the default
Native CAD deliverableBoth✓✓—
Sketch and timeline rulesBoth✓✓—
Photo use and detailBoth✓✓—
Window walls 1.75 not 1.4Fable only✓——
Fit toleranceFable only✓——
Width and height wordingFable only✓——
Guard position in ZOpus only—✓—
Handle edge roundingOpus only—✓—
Stem root filletOpus only—✓—
Thin web vs 4 perimetersOpus only—✓—
Who saw whatFable’s extra catches are about reading the numbers closely (window walls, fit tolerance, the word “height”). Opus’s extra catches lean toward the printed part (stem root strength, thin web versus perimeters, handle edges, where the guard sits in Z).
#TopicIssueWorkaround applied
1Stem lengthThe three distances add up to 33.5, not 34.0stem_length is computed as the sum, 33.5 mm (Swami’s decision)
2DeliverableA browser page cannot write Fusion or STEP solidsSTL and quad OBJ, plus a parameter CSV for Fusion; a native Fusion model can be a separate thread (Swami’s decision)
3Sketch rulesThese are Fusion timeline terms with no direct meaning for a mesh generatorMet in spirit: one parameter list, formula-placed features, half built and mirrored, guard face as datum
4Stem recessNot said which faces are recessed or where the recess starts and endsRecessed equally on both faces (Swami’s decision), from 1.4 mm off the guard to 1.4 mm before the window; stem_recess_start is adjustable
5Rim applied twiceThe same 1.4 rim is used as wall width and as recess depth per faceTaken literally: 1.4 mm wall around the outline and 1.4 mm deep recess on each face, leaving a 1.3 mm web
6Window wallsThe window is narrower than the web, so the walls beside it are 1.75, not 1.4Accepted as written; the window zone is left at full thickness
7Diamond tipUnclear whether the diamond is seen from the side, from above, or is a raised markDefault: thickness thins from 4.1 to a 2.6 nose over 5.5 mm; stem_tip_style offers a width taper or a flat tip
8Side notchA 3-point arc already returns to the edge, so the taper has nothing to taper from; side not statedTeardrop on both edges: the arc, then a tangent ramp reaching the edge at 22.0
9Chamfer scopeWhich edges count as leading is not listedTip corners in plan and the nose in thickness; the long edges and the window stay sharp
10Guard edgesNo sizes given2.0 mm corner radius and 0.5 mm bevel, both adjustable
11Handle outlineThe arc shape and the meaning of the transition zone are openFull width for 5.0 mm with 5.0 mm rounded back corners, then one tangent arc (radius 27.82 mm) to 12.0; three other curve styles offered
12Handle thicknessWhere and how it tapers is not saidSame zone and curve family as the outline; style adjustable separately
13Handle lengthNot said whether it includes the guardMeasured from the back of the guard; overall length is 24.0 + 3.0 + 33.5 = 60.5 mm
14Grip textureNo count, size, direction or positionGrooves across both faces, 1.2 wide, 0.6 deep, 2.2 apart, clear of the hole; all adjustable
15Lanyard holeHole direction not statedThrough the thickness, at the middle of the handle length; an offset parameter moves it
16Print flatA key symmetric about its mid-plane touches the bed only under the handle; the stem sits 6.45 mm above itGeometry kept symmetric per spec; supports under the guard and stem are needed (see Print and Test)
17Fit toleranceNo clearance for the switch barrel or for print shrinkageNone applied; stem_width and stem_thickness are the two values to trim after a test print
18Width and height wordsHeight means the same direction for both, but it is easy to misreadHeight is treated as thickness (Z) everywhere; width is across the key (Y)
19PhotosOne composite photo of the original key, no scale referenceUsed only to confirm the general layout; all sizes come from the spec
#TopicKindIssueWorkaround applied
1Stem lengthConflict22.0 + 6.0 + 5.5 (window start + window + tip distance) is 33.5, not 34.0. The spec contradicts itself.Used 33.5 mm (Swami's ruling). stem_length is now derived from the three dimensions, so it can never disagree again.
2RecessAmbiguityThe rim is a width, but the formula also uses it as a depth on both faces. Which faces carry the recess is not said.Recess on both faces (Swami's ruling), each 1.4 mm deep, leaving the 1.3 mm web. A control allows 0, 1 or 2 faces.
3RecessAmbiguityWhere the recess starts and stops along the stem is not given, nor whether it surrounds the window.Recess runs from 1.4 mm in front of the guard to 1.4 mm before the window, inside the 1.4 mm rim. The window block and the tip stay solid so the latch bears on full 4.1 mm material, as on the OEM key in the photo.
4Print layoutConflictA key symmetric about its mid-plane cannot print flat in one piece: with a 17 mm handle and a 4.1 mm blade, the blade would float 6.45 mm above the bed (the Thingiverse model splits in two for this reason).Default 'flat underside': every part's underside rests on Z = 0, so it prints in one piece with no supports. Left/right symmetry is kept. An 'OEM centred' switch restores the mid-plane layout.
5Diamond tipAmbiguityNot said whether the diamond is in plan, in side view, a raised emboss or the whole tip; 2.6 mm is narrower than the 4.1 mm thickness.The last 5.5 mm tapers in plan from 9.5 mm to a 2.6 mm flat nose (an arrow point) for self-centring. Taper length and nose width are parameters.
6Diamond tipAmbiguityThe two 5.5 mm values coincide, so the taper starts exactly at the window's front edge, leaving no straight section in front of the window.Kept as written; the solid front bar is still 5.5 mm long and the window's side walls are 1.75 mm. A separate tip length control lets the taper start later.
7Side notchAmbiguityWhether 14.0 mm is the start or the middle of the arc, which of the 3 points are meant, and whether one or both edges are cut are not given.14.0 mm is where the cut begins (same convention as stem_cutout_start). Arc from 14 to 18 mm reaching 1.0 mm deep, tangent at the bottom (R 8.5 mm), then a straight taper back to a point at 22 mm. Cut on both edges for symmetry.
8Side notchAmbiguityThe 1.0 mm notch would leave only 0.4 mm of rim where it overlaps the recess.The recess edge follows the notch, so the rim stays a full 1.4 mm wide everywhere.
9ChamferAmbiguityWhich edges count as leading is not listed; chamfering the window would weaken the latch.0.5 mm 45-degree chamfer on all outer stem edges (top and bottom) and the nose, plus the nose corners in plan. Window edges left sharp. A switch limits it to the tip only.
10GuardMissing detailNo radius or bevel size given; radius or bevel not chosen.R2.0 on the four corners of the 18 x 11 face and R0.5 on every face edge, both parameters.
11GuardMissing detailIts position relative to the stem and handle in Z is not stated.Centred on the stem in the OEM layout; bottom-aligned with the stem in the flat-underside layout. X = 0 is the guard's stem-side face.
12Handle outlineAmbiguityThe arc radius, where the 27 mm is reached and what the 'rounded edge transition zone' is are not defined.A 5 mm straight neck at 12 mm, then a concave arc tangent to the neck and to an R4 butt corner, reaching 27 mm at the butt. The arc radius (14.75 mm) is solved from those constraints.
13Handle thicknessMissing detailThe thickness profile along the handle is not given.Smooth S-curve from 9.5 mm at the guard to 17 mm at 70% of the handle length, then level to the butt. The peak position is a parameter.
14Handle edgesMissing detailNo edge rounding is specified for the handle.R2.5 round on every handle edge, measured from the true outline so the flare and corners round evenly.
15Grip ribsMissing detailCount, size, spacing, direction and even which faces 'thickness faces' means are not given.Transverse rounded grooves (across the pull direction) on both broad faces: 1.2 mm wide, 0.6 mm deep, 2.2 mm pitch, faded out in the edge rounds. All four are parameters.
16Lanyard holeConflictCentred along the length puts the hole in the middle of the grip area, so ribs and hole compete for space.Hole at the handle's mid-length (X = -15 mm) with a 0.5 mm chamfer on both faces; ribs placed either side of it (4 per face). An offset control moves the hole.
17Handle lengthMissing detailNot said where it is measured from.Measured from the guard's back face to the butt; overall key length 60.5 mm.
18DeliverableScopeThis entry is a browser-based mesh generator, not a CAD timeline.Per Swami: STL and quad OBJ now; a Fusion model may be a separate entry. The full parameter set exports as JSON and is listed in the Parameter Table.
19Parametric CADScopeSketch constraints and a Fusion timeline do not exist in a mesh generator.Equivalent intent: every dimension is a named live parameter, derived values are computed, and the mesh is rebuilt deterministically from them on each change.
20Stem rootMissing detailNo fillet is specified where the stem meets the guard, the most stressed spot when pulled by the lanyard.Left sharp to keep the full stem length usable in the barrel; flagged in the Print and Test Guide as the first place to check.
21Photo detailScopeNeither is in the spec.Not modelled; the spec's grip ribs take the pocket's place.
22Thin webNoteThe 1.3 mm web and 1.4 mm rims are thinner than 4 perimeters, so infill never reaches them.No change needed: those areas print as solid perimeters, which is stronger. Noted in the Print and Test Guide.
10VerdictVERDICT▶
  • UsageOpus 5.5 did the same job for about a quarter to a third of the 5-hour session usage (4 points against 14) and well under half the weekly usage.
  • SpeedOpus was faster at both milestones: first model about 2 minutes sooner, published about 8.5 minutes sooner.
  • OutputBoth keys are watertight, spec-sized and fully parametric. Opus defaults to a support-free print; Fable keeps the OEM symmetric shape and needs supports.
  • Spec readingClose to a tie: 16 shared topics, with each model catching a few the other missed.
  • Fable resetsThree free Fable resets (until Mar 9, 2027) can refund a Fable run’s session and weekly usage, which narrows the cost gap while they last.
  • CaveatOne run each, whole-number readings and no test print yet. A second pair of runs, or the print test, would firm up the call.
One lineOn this task, Opus 5.5 at medium thinking matched Fable 5.2’s output for roughly 3.5 times less session usage and in about 70% of the time.

12GlossaryREFERENCE▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section. Each term’s Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
5-hour session limitPlan LimitsThe rolling usage limit on a Claude plan that refills five hours after a session starts; the usage page shows it as a percentage used.
Weekly limitPlan LimitsThe plan-wide usage cap that resets once a week (Sunday 2:00 AM for Swami); shown as a percentage used.
Full resetPlan LimitsA one-off free reset of the plan limits, shown on the usage page with its own expiry date.
Fable allowancePlan LimitsA separate usage allowance for the Fable model that a Fable reset refills; its meter was not in the screenshots.
Percentage pointPlan LimitsOne percent of a limit. A move from 14% to 18% used is 4 points.
Claude MaxProductsThe Claude subscription plan Swami uses; its limits are what this page measures.
Claude CodeProductsThe coding agent product; both runs were Claude Code threads, so they show up in its share of weekly usage.
CoworkProductsClaude’s desktop work product; its share of the week should stay flat during the runs, which makes it a rounding check.
Fable 5.2ModelsThe Claude model that built the first entry; it has its own allowance and reset type.
Opus 5.5ModelsThe Claude model that built the second entry.
Medium thinkingModelsThe reasoning effort setting both runs used; higher effort usually costs more usage.
WatertightMeshA mesh with no holes or open edges, so a slicer can tell inside from outside.
GenusMeshThe number of through-holes in a closed shape; the key has two, the lanyard hole and the locking window.
Quad OBJMeshAn OBJ mesh file made mostly of four-sided faces, easier to edit in modelling tools than triangles.
STLMeshThe standard triangle-mesh file for 3D printing.
3MFMeshA 3D printing file that can carry colours and materials per part along with the mesh.
Flat undersidePrintingOpus’s default layout: every part’s underside sits on the print bed, so the key prints in one piece without supports.
OEM centredPrintingThe layout of the original key, symmetric about its mid-plane; the blade then floats above the bed and needs supports.
PETGPrintingThe plastic the spec calls for: tough, slightly flexible, good for outdoor parts.
Spec issueBenchmarkAn ambiguity, conflict or missing detail in Izzy’s specification, logged with the workaround applied, as the benchmark requires.
Parametric generatorBenchmarkA page that rebuilds the key live from a list of dimensions, so any value can change without remodelling.
